S4.01.note: Empty-state and composer exist in code; not run.
steps: Sign in, then open AGI Code from the activity bar (or run Code: Open Chat).
Click the + button whose tooltip is "New chat".
Look for an empty chat with a composer that says "Describe a task…" and type a first message to start a new conversation.
S4.01.where: AGI Code sidebar > New chat (+ button in the header, tooltip "New chat"); command palette: Code: New Conversation

S4.02.needs: a signed-in account with at least one past session
S4.02.note: The plan's Code line pointed at commandSetup.ts:1243 (now the sign-out handler). The open-session command is agi-workforce.openConversation at apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1392.
steps: Click the history icon with tooltip "Sessions" in the AGI Code header.
Click one session in the list.
Check that its transcript opens and that you can send a new message to continue it.
S4.02.where: AGI Code sidebar > Sessions (history icon in the header) > click a session row; command palette: Code: Open Conversation

S4.03.needs: a signed-in account with several past sessions
S4.03.note: The quick-pick version says "Search sessions by title or message text" (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json). Whether the sheet box matches message text was not verified in code.
steps: Click the "Sessions" icon in the AGI Code header.
Click the "Search sessions" box and type a word from a session title.
Clear it and type a word that appears only inside a message body.
Click a matching result and check it opens that session.
S4.03.where: AGI Code sidebar > Sessions (history icon) > Search sessions box; also command palette: Code: Show Sessions History

S4.04.needs: a signed-in account with at least one archived session
steps: Click "Sessions" in the AGI Code header.
Click the archive icon labelled "Archived sessions".
Select a session and click the Restore button, or the Delete permanently button.
Confirm the delete prompt if you chose it; check the session is back in the list or gone from the archive.
S4.04.where: AGI Code sidebar > Sessions (history icon) > Archived sessions (archive icon); command palette: Code: Archived Sessions

steps: Click the "More" button in the AGI Code header.
Click "Projects".
Check the list opens with the placeholder "Open a project…".
Click the "New project" icon in the list's title bar and check the create flow starts.
S4.06.where: AGI Code header > More (…) > Projects; command palette: Code: Show Projects

S4.07.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project
S4.07.note: The project home is a quick-pick list, not a full page.
steps: Click "More" in the AGI Code header, then "Projects".
Click a project in the list.
Check the project home shows its name, an "About" section with description and instructions, "Knowledge files" and "Recent conversations".
S4.07.where: AGI Code header > More > Projects > click a project

S4.08.needs: a signed-in account with a project that has conversations
S4.08.note: Selecting a conversation calls vscode.env.openExternal, so it opens outside the editor.
steps: Open a project from More > Projects.
Scroll to the "Recent conversations" section.
Click one conversation.
Check that it opens; the code opens it in the web app in the browser, not inside the editor.
S4.08.where: AGI Code header > More > Projects > click a project > "Recent conversations" section > click a conversation

S4.10.needs: a signed-in account with a project
S4.10.note: Settings > Instructions & editor holds workspace custom instructions, not per-project ones. The effect on chats was not verified in code.
steps: Open a project from More > Projects.
Under "Edit", click "Instructions".
Change the text in the "Project instructions" box and save.
Reopen the project and check the saved text shows; check it is used in a chat in that project.
S4.10.where: AGI Code header > More > Projects > click a project > Edit > Instructions

S4.14.needs: a signed-in account with cloud tasks
S4.14.note: No dedicated filter for finished tasks was found; finished work sits in the Done and Stopped groups.
steps: Click "More" in the AGI Code header, then "Work".
Read the groups "Needs you", "Working", "Ready for review", "Done" and "Stopped".
To hide finished work, type a word in the list's box to narrow it; no separate filter toggle was found.
Compare each task's status text with what is shown on the cloud web app.

S4.15.needs: a signed-in account with a cloud task
S4.15.note: The detail is a quick-pick list. A step-by-step transcript appears only for coding sessions (cloudCodeSessions.ts).
steps: Click "More", then "Work".
Click a task under any group.
Read the sections "Progress", "Outcome", "Result", "Error", "Outputs" (only those that apply).
Check the "Actions" section for approve or reject when a decision is pending.
S4.15.where: AGI Code header > More > Work > click a cloud task row

S4.16.needs: a signed-in account with a cloud task waiting for approval
S4.16.note: "Needs you" acts as the cross-task inbox. "Code: Show Approval History" is a record of past approvals, not the pending list.
steps: Click "More", then "Work".
Look in the "Needs you" group for tasks waiting on you.
On a row, click the check icon "Approve this run" or the x icon "Reject this run".
Open a task and use "Approve" or "Reject" in its Actions section, then check the row leaves "Needs you".
S4.16.where: AGI Code header > More > Work > "Needs you" group; approve or reject on the row, or open the task > Actions

S4.18.needs: a signed-in account with at least one schedule
S4.18.note: Clicking the row itself opens the schedules page on the web (agi-workforce.openSchedule), not an in-app detail page.
steps: Run "Code: Show Schedules" from the command palette.
Hover a schedule row to read its status, cadence, timezone, next run and prompt in the tooltip.
Click the history icon "Show recent runs" on the row.
Check the run list matches Expected: runs with their status and times.
S4.18.where: Command palette > Code: Show Schedules; then hover a schedule row, or use its "Show recent runs" icon

S4.19.note: No dedicated coding-session home found. Closest: the Sessions sheet with its Local and Cloud tabs plus the + New chat button (webviewContent.ts), and Code: Session Worktrees > New session in a worktree (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/sessionWorktrees.ts). Searched the app folder for a coding home, coding sessions and repository-start screens.

S4.20.needs: a signed-in account with a coding session that changed files
S4.20.note: No separate workspace screen found; the sidebar chat panel is the workspace. Diff controls are commands such as Code: Accept Diff.
steps: Click "Sessions" in the AGI Code header and open a session.
Read the transcript in the chat panel.
Where a change exists, click "Review changes".
Type your next instruction in the box that says "Describe a task…" and check the reply continues the session.
S4.20.where: AGI Code header > Sessions > open a session row (the chat panel is the workspace)

S4.25.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact
steps: Click "More" in the AGI Code header, then "Artifacts".
Check the list of your artifacts.
Click one artifact and check it opens.
S4.25.where: AGI Code header > More > Artifacts; command palette: Code: Show Artifacts

S4.35.note: The remove control uses a shared constant; its visible word was not checked.
steps: Click "More", then "Skills".
Check the installed and available lists.
Click "Install a skill" or "Create a skill" from the top of the list.
On a skill row, use the "Turn on" or "Turn off" button and check the state changes.
S4.35.where: AGI Code header > More > Skills; also Settings > Integrations > Skills

S4.36.needs: a signed-in account to browse the marketplace
S4.36.note: The remove control is not checked for its visible word.
steps: Click "More", then "Plugins".
Check the installed plugins and the "Browse AGI Cloud Marketplace" entry.
Click "Install a plugin" to add one.
On an installed plugin, use "Configure options" or "Update" and check the result.
S4.36.where: AGI Code header > More > Plugins; also Settings > Integrations > Plugins

S4.39.needs: a paid account to see plan windows (a Free account sees only the Upgrade item)
S4.39.note: Usage is a quick-pick list. Plan windows are session, weekly and credits as the data provides them.
steps: Click "More", then the "Account & usage" item (or run the command).
Read "Session usage" and the "<plan> plan usage" rows with their reset times.
Scroll to "Usage history" for recent usage.
S4.39.where: AGI Code header > More > Account & usage; command palette: Code: Account & usage

S4.41.note: No profile, appearance or notification sections were found in code; only About you and Responses exist here.
steps: Click "More", then "Personalization".
Under "About you", pick "What should AGI call you?" and change it.
Under "Responses", change "Style" or "Length".
Close and reopen Personalization and check the new values are kept.
S4.41.where: AGI Code header > More > Personalization; command palette: Code: Personalization

S4.44.needs: a signed-in account to send feedback
S4.44.note: Help menu is in helpMenu.ts; the Code line's submitFeedback.ts was not the menu.
steps: Click "More", then "Help".
Check the items "Help center", "Service status", "Documentation", "Contact support" open web pages.
Click "Send feedback", then choose "Report a Bug" and check the feedback form opens.
